sections.heading: Get started with AgentShield
body: AgentShield gives tenant administrators and developers one place to manage API access, route model requests, and review usage and service health.

sections.heading: API keys
body: Create a tenant key from [API keys & access](/keys). Give it a recognizable name, copy the secret when it is shown, and store it in a secret manager. The portal does not show the full secret again. Revoke keys that are no longer needed. Key creation and rotation are restricted to permissions held by the signed-in principal.

sections.heading: Make your first request
body: Send requests through the gateway using a tenant key in the `X-Tenant-API-Key` header. Use a model configured for your workspace; model names and providers are managed in [Models & routing](/models).
For the Meta model hosted through Baseten, configure `META_API_BASE_URL` and `BASETEN_API_KEY` for the gateway. The request uses the OpenAI-compatible chat completion shape:

The gateway authenticates the tenant, applies configured ingress guardrails, and forwards eligible requests to the configured provider. Never put provider credentials in browser code or send them from a client.

sections.heading: Usage and service health
body: Open [Overview](/dashboard) for tenant usage and the current service health summary. Open [Observability](/logs) to review recent gateway events. A degraded or stale health result means the latest probe needs attention; check the service detail before treating it as recovered.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
body: An authentication error usually means the key is missing, invalid, revoked, or sent in the wrong header. A permission error means the signed-in principal does not hold the required permission. A degraded service means a dependency probe failed or became stale; review its reported detail and the [Observability](/logs) page.
For API request and response schemas, use the gateway's API documentation at `/api/docs` in a running local deployment.

sections.heading: Make your first request
sections.body:
Send requests through the gateway using a tenant key in the `X-Tenant-API-Key` header. Use a model configured for your workspace; model names and providers are managed in [Models & routing](/models).

For the Meta model hosted through Baseten, configure `META_API_BASE_URL` and `BASETEN_API_KEY` for the gateway. The request uses the OpenAI-compatible chat completion shape:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/meta/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Tenant-API-Key: <YOUR_TENANT_API_KEY>' \
  -d '{"model":"<CONFIGURED_META_MODEL>","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}'
```

The gateway authenticates the tenant, applies configured ingress guardrails, and forwards eligible requests to the configured provider. Never put provider credentials in browser code or send them from a client.

AC-5: Retrieve usage summary for authenticated tenant.

Cost fields are populated only for a principal holding billing:admin and
stay null for everyone else, so usage is never withheld from a tenant
member who cannot see spend (Spec 0011 AC-2, AC-6).

Key management requires `keys:write`, and a principal may only grant scopes it
holds itself, so no credential can mint a successor more privileged than the
caller (spec 0012 review blocker).

sections.title: AgentShield API
sections.heading: Update Api Key Scopes
sections.summary:
Set the scope list of an existing key.

This is the write behind the portal's "Manage" control on a key row: a
credential's permissions are the only access state this gateway stores, so
rescoping is how access is actually managed. It is a key write, so it needs
`keys:write`, and the escalation rule that governs creation governs this
too: a principal may only grant scopes it holds, or a key manager could mint
itself privileges it never held by editing a key it did control.

The read-check-write runs under WATCH on the tenant key hash so a concurrent
rotation cannot be overwritten by a stale copy of its metadata.

`keys:write`, and the escalation rule that governs creation governs this
too: a principal may only grant scopes it holds, or a key manager could mint
itself privileges it never held by editing a key it did control.

sections.title: AgentShield API
sections.heading: Execute a tenant tool
sections.summary:
Invoke a tool registered on the MCP server on behalf of the authenticated tenant.

The endpoint calls the standard MCP streamable transport. Requires the `tools:execute` scope.
A principal without it receives `403` and an authz failure event is emitted
to telemetry. The W3C `traceparent` header is forwarded to the MCP server and
echoed back as `trace_id`.
sections.body:

sections.title: AgentShield API
sections.heading: Run a guarded chat completion
sections.summary:
Send a prompt or message history to the model under the tenant's guardrails.

Requests are scanned for prompt injection, checked against the tenant quota and
daily budget, served from the semantic cache when possible, and metered. Returns
`402` when the daily budget is exhausted and `429` when the rate limit is hit.
